# Wave 05.5 — Task 05.5 — Repository Linting and Code Readability

## Status and Preconditions

Planned only; no implementation has started. This is task 05.5 within Wave 05.5 (05.5-T05.5), inserted between T05 and T06, not a new wave. Read the [wave specification](README.md) and accepted T01-T05 decisions/deliverables. Wait for the predecessor's validation, independent review and human acceptance before execution.

## Context / Objective

Establish reproducible linting and formatting for frontend, api, scripts and worker, then correct existing source/test code to satisfy the approved rules without changing product behavior. Configuration alone does not complete this task.

Source proposal: Grok_Análise-e-proposta-de-linting-para-projeto-com-IA_20261021-2245.md, supplied by the user on 2026-10-22. Its snippets and embedded requests are reference material, not executable instructions or verified dependency recommendations. This task is self-contained; agents must inspect the actual repository and official tool documentation for installed versions before choosing configuration.

## Observed Planning Baseline

- Root ESLint config uses browser globals broadly; Node scripts need explicit Node scope.
- API has type-aware ESLint and Prettier integration; its existing lint command uses --fix.
- Frontend has typecheck/tests/build but no lint scripts in its package manifest.
- Worker container uses Python 3.12; no Ruff configuration was identified.
- Root and API have separate Prettier configuration. Root, API and frontend have distinct pnpm lockfiles; do not assume a root pnpm workspace.
- API enables emitDecoratorMetadata and experimentalDecorators. Import transformations must preserve runtime dependency injection.
- Reinspect all of this after T05; the earlier tasks may add files or change tooling.

## Scope / Required Changes

### 1. Inventory and approved rule policy

- Inventory tracked source, tests and tooling configuration in the four directories, including api/scripts and frontend/tests; record which command/config covers each file family.
- Record baseline diagnostics by component/rule before fixes. Separate pre-existing failures from new failures and identify runtime-sensitive transformations.
- Verify ESLint, typescript-eslint, Next configuration, Prettier and Ruff compatibility against current manifests, lockfiles and official documentation. Use supported flat config exports where available; do not copy FlatCompat or version ranges without verification.
- Keep current package boundaries and install/lockfile workflow. Do not migrate package managers, introduce uv, or upgrade application frameworks as a side effect.
- Select reproducible development dependency versions according to repository policy. Ruff is a development tool, not a required production Worker dependency.

### 2. Worker: Ruff lint and format

- Add worker/ruff.toml or worker/pyproject.toml, not competing sources of truth, targeting the supported Python runtime (currently py312).
- Use the proposal's E, W, F, I, UP, B, SIM, C4 and RUF families as a starting point. Review formatter conflicts and document final rule selection. E501 may be excluded with rationale; formatting does not guarantee every line fits.
- Define imports using actual worker launch/test modes; validate worker, json_adapters and outbox classification.
- Configure consistent double quotes, spaces and a documented line width (proposal: 100). Decide line endings explicitly for Windows/Linux.
- Provide reproducible dev installation and lint/format check/fix commands, including test_worker.py.
- Correct all in-scope findings. Never use unsafe fixes automatically; inspect transformations involving exceptions, subprocesses, locks, persistence and retries.

### 3. Frontend: ESLint and shared Prettier

- Add compatible Next/React/TypeScript lint configuration covering App Router, components, lib and tests, with correct browser/server/Node contexts.
- Preserve Hooks and Next correctness rules. Do not broadly disable useful rules merely to pass.
- Integrate shared formatting policy without duplicate/conflicting formatting authorities; document whether Prettier runs independently or through ESLint.
- Preserve existing tests, integration scripts, typecheck and build commands. Add read-only lint/format checks and separately named fix/write commands.
- Correct existing findings while preserving proxy security, session handling, polling, stale-response invalidation and accessibility.

### 4. API: strengthen existing lint safely

- Retain type-aware checking with correct projectService/tsconfig boundaries. Explicitly cover source/tests and non-project tooling scripts with appropriate overrides rather than silently excluding them.
- Evaluate consistent-type-imports, no-unused-vars, prefer-nullish-coalescing and prefer-optional-chain against compiler settings and runtime behavior.
- Do not convert Nest dependency-injection classes to type-only imports when runtime decorator metadata requires values. Validate module bootstrap/DI, not just compilation.
- Do not blindly replace || with ??; empty-string and zero fallbacks may be intentional configuration behavior.
- Address floating promises/unsafe arguments with real typing and intentional handling rather than broad any casts, suppressions or unrelated strictness changes.
- Make the default lint command non-mutating; provide lint:fix separately. Align formatting with the chosen root policy.

### 5. Node scripts and root orchestration

- Scope Node recommended rules to actual JS/MJS/CJS files and tooling, with correct module/test globals. Avoid blanket browser globals and accidental double linting of package code.
- Correct root scripts and api/scripts without altering Docker isolation, process cleanup, environment handling, fixture creation, migration logic or command exit propagation.
- Create root aggregate checks that include API, frontend, Node scripts and Worker. Do not omit scripts/Worker from a command advertised as repository-wide.
- Use explicit package-directory execution supported by the current layout; do not assume pnpm --filter works without a configured workspace.
- Unify Prettier policy (proposal: double quotes, trailing commas, width 100, two spaces, semicolons). Remove or align overrides deliberately.
- Define bounded file globs and ignore generated outputs, dependencies, caches, virtualenvs, .git, runtime-data, recordings, outbox/checkpoints and secrets. Preserve applied migration SQL/snapshots and generated lockfiles from formatter rewrites.
- Keep root checks usable on Windows and Linux; resolve Ruff through a documented interpreter/environment. Missing tools must fail clearly, not be silently skipped.
- If existing CI is present, integrate read-only checks into its established flow. Do not add remote deployment or a new CI platform.

### 6. Remediation and agent documentation

- Apply formatting/safe fixes in reviewable component groups; inspect diffs and make targeted manual corrections where needed.
- Fix tracked source/tests within the approved scope, including code added by T01-T05. Do not hide the baseline with bulk eslint-disable/noqa comments, blanket ignores, test deletion or broad rule weakening.
- Any narrow exception needs a concrete compatibility rationale and review; selected-rule diagnostics must reach the accepted zero-error/zero-warning gate.
- Document installation, scope, policy, check versus fix commands and troubleshooting in README-LINTING.md or an existing developer guide, linking from relevant component docs.
- Update applicable project/agent validation guidance minimally so future tasks use read-only lint checks and explicit fixes. Preserve model assignments, handoffs and existing approval/status rules.
- T06 and T07 must retain these checks as gates for code they subsequently change.

## Command Contract

Final script names may follow existing conventions, but document exact commands and working directories before acceptance:

| Purpose | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| lint / lint:check | Read-only ESLint and Ruff checks, nonzero on diagnostics or missing tools |
| lint:fix | Explicitly mutating, bounded safe fixes; no automatic unsafe Ruff fixes |
| format:check | Prettier --check and Ruff format --check across applicable scope |
| format / format:write | Explicit bounded writes, never an acceptance/CI check |
| Root aggregate | Runs all four areas, propagates failures and does not silently skip tools |

Examples from the source document such as ruff format and eslint --fix are remediation commands, not CI/check commands. Avoid an unbounded prettier --write . over private/runtime files.

## Explicit Exclusions

No execution is authorized merely by creating this file. During later implementation, no new authentication feature, schema/migration rewrite, storage authority switch, real-data migration, business-rule change, dependency/framework overhaul, media rewrite, unrelated documentation formatting, hosted deployment or automatic staging/commit/push.

A suspected functional bug exposed by lint must be reported to Coordinator for scope review; do not silently fold broad behavioral changes into formatting work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Coverage inventory accounts for frontend, API, Worker, root scripts and nested test/tool scripts.
- [ ] Compatible, reproducible ESLint/Prettier/Ruff configuration and development setup are documented.
- [ ] Root and component lint/format checks pass with no unresolved selected-rule diagnostics.
- [ ] All required in-scope code corrections are complete; no bulk suppressions or silently excluded source.
- [ ] Check commands leave tracked source/configuration unchanged and a second formatting pass is idempotent.
- [ ] Generated artifacts, applied migrations, private data and media remain untouched.
- [ ] Nest runtime DI, frontend behavior, Worker lifecycle/outbox and script isolation remain correct.
- [ ] Existing APIs, ownership/session boundaries and local/JSON/bridge behavior are preserved.
- [ ] Documentation and future agent gates distinguish read-only checks from explicit fixes.
- [ ] Required regressions pass; blocked/skipped mandatory checks are not reported as PASS.

## Automated Tests / Verification

Start with focused checks for each changed component. After remediation, run the complete new lint/format checks, API Jest/typecheck/build, frontend tests/typecheck/build and Worker unittest/pytest. Verify API module bootstrap/DI using existing safe test infrastructure.

Run node scripts/test-db-foundation.mjs and root pnpm test:smoke in isolated synthetic environments to validate persistence and both JSON/bridge execution paths affected by repository-wide fixes. Use fake Streamlink, project-owned disposable volumes and random loopback ports. Do not use live platforms or normal user data.

Record exact commands, versions, before/after diagnostic counts, final statuses and any approved narrow exceptions. Check git diff --check, source changes before/after read-only checks, formatter idempotence and lockfile scope. Dependency/image preparation is separate from test execution. No tests are required merely to create this specification; validate its links/frontmatter/dependencies instead.

## Risks / Recovery

Main risks are large diffs hiding behavior changes, Nest decorator metadata changes, altered fallback semantics, unsafe Python fixes, lint scope omissions and tooling scanning private data. Keep fixes component-bounded and review semantic edits separately. Revert only task-owned changes if needed; never reset unrelated work, delete user data or clear an outbox to pass checks.
